newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan money data shows gradual recovery - economists.
newsitem.headline: Japan money data shows gradual recovery - economists.

text.p: The 3.7 percent growth in Japan's money supply in August showed that the economy was continuing to recover gradually, economists said on Wednesday.

The Bank of Japan said earlier that Japan's broadly defined money supply average of M2 plus certificates of deposit (CDs), a key gauge of money supply, grew a preliminary 3.7 percent year on year in August, compared with a revised 3.7 percent rise in July.
"Money supply is showing only slight movement, which reflects the current state of the economy," said Ryo Sawai, an economist for the Yamaichi Research Institute.
Seiji Adachi, an economist for Daiwa Institute of Research, said the August money supply data showed that the economy was recovering gradually.
The stagnation of the money supply was due to a lack of growth in fund demand from corporations overall, economists said.
Money supply growth may decline in the next few months along with the economy, Yamaichi's Sawai added.
"I expect money supply to fall somewhat on a year-on-year basis in the next few months. The pace of economic recovery may also slow down toward the end of the year," he said.
